No rule in the formula-audit table governs outgoing damage amplification ("increased damage from all sources"); the document only defines mitigation m(R)=100/(100+R), penetration order, and the audited engine families. The amp value therefore has to come from the cached wiki text, which it does.

independent_computation.step_1_template_semantics: The League Wiki template {{rd|A|B}} renders a melee/ranged split with the MELEE value first and the RANGED value second. Calibrated against three items whose split is independently known: Death's Dance {{rd|30%|10%}} (melee stores 30%, ranged 10%), Ravenous Hydra / Tiamat / Stridebreaker Cleave {{rd|40% AD|20% AD}} (ranged is the halved value), Blade of the Ruined King {{rd|9%|6%}} (melee 9% current health, ranged 6%). In every cached instance the second argument is the smaller, ranged-nerfed number (e.g. Doran's Shield {{rd|0 to 5 for 11|0 to 3.75 for 11}} = ranged at 75%).
independent_computation.step_2_read_the_value: Bloodsong's Expose Weakness debuff therefore causes the affected champion to take 8% increased damage from all sources when the Bloodsong holder is MELEE, and 5% when the holder is RANGED. Duration 4 s, 1.5 s internal cooldown, applied only when the Spellblade-empowered attack hits a champion.
independent_computation.step_3_to_a_multiplier: An 'X% increased damage taken' debuff is an outgoing-damage amplifier of the multiplicative form multiplier = 1 + X/100. Melee holder: 1 + 8/100 = 1.08. Ranged holder: 1 + 5/100 = 1.05.
independent_computation.result: support_damage_multiplier = 1.08 (melee Bloodsong holder) | 1.05 (ranged Bloodsong holder). Absent / 1.0 is not a value the source text can produce for an event that carries the Expose Weakness debuff.
independent_computation.check_on_the_old_value: The old state (<absent>) asserts no amplification at all on an event whose own source string is 'Bloodsong — Expose Weakness'. The cached item text is unambiguous that a champion hit by the Spellblade proc takes increased damage for 4 seconds, so an absent multiplier is wrong under any reading of the source.

residual_uncertainty.statement: The one input the permitted evidence tree cannot supply is the range type of the Bloodsong holder in this scenario's roster: the scenario definition lives outside data/ and docs/math-foundations.md (data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json does not contain 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster', and no data/ file names the roster).
residual_uncertainty.consequence: 1.08 is exactly right for a melee Bloodsong holder; 1.05 would be the correct leaf for a ranged holder. 1.08 is a literal value of the cached source text, so the new value is correct on the melee branch and is in any case strictly closer to the source than the old absent value.
residual_uncertainty.how_a_reviewer_can_close_it: Confirm the Bloodsong-carrying ally in the 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' scenario is a melee champion; if it is ranged, the leaf should read 1.05 with the same source string.

verdict_rationale: 1 + 8/100 = 1.08 reproduces the melee branch of {{rd|8%|5%}} in the cached Bloodsong wiki text exactly, with the standard 1 + X/100 form for an 'increased damage taken' amplifier. The old value (<absent>, i.e. no amplification) is inconsistent with the same source text and is wrong.
